<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par68 />(but never in the 1st ''sing.'' {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֹמַר}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֹכַל}}), and then the final syllable, if without the {{GHGterm|pause}}, always takes {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַ֫יֹּאמֶר|translate=and he said}} (except {{GHGheb|text=וַתֹּ֫אמַר לוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=7|verse=13}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|68|e}}
In {{GHGterm|pause}}, however, the {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}} (except the 1st pers. of {{GHGheb|text=אָכַל}}, see below) always has the form {{GHGheb|text=וַיֹּאכַ֫ל}} (but ''plur.'' always {{GHGheb|text=יֹאכֵ֫לוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיֹּאכֵ֫לוּ}}), {{GHGheb|text=וַיֹּאמַ֫ר}}; except {{GHGheb|text=וַיֹּ֫אמַר}} in the poetic portion of the book of Job, as 3:2, 4:1, &c., but not in 32:6, in the middle of the verse. The weak {{GHGterm|imperfect}} of {{GHGheb|text=אָחַז}} is always {{GHGheb|text=יֹאחֵז}} and {{GHGheb|text=וַיֹּאחֶז}}, but in the 1st ''sing.'', according to {{GHGpar|49|e}}, {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֹחֵ֫ז}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=6}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֹכֵ֫ל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn.|chapter=3|verse=12.13}} in {{GHGterm|pause}}.—{{GHGheb|text=אָבָה}} and {{GHGheb|text=אָפָה}} are, at the same time, verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, hence {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יֹּאבֶה}} ({{GHGpar|75|c}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|68|f}}
Before ''light'' suffixes the vowel of the second syllable becomes vocal Šewâ, as {{GHGheb|text=יֹֽאכְלֵם}}, {{GHGheb|text=תֹּֽאכְלֶ֫נּוּ}} but {{GHGheb|text=תֹּֽאכַלְכֶם}}.—In a few cases, instead of the ''ô'' in the first syllable an ''ê'' is found, which is due to contraction from the group {{GHGheb|text=־ֶֽ ־ֱ}} (or {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ ־ְ}}) in place of {{GHGheb|text=־ַ ־ְ }}; e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תֵּאתֶה|translate=it shall come}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=4|verse=8}}, from {{GHGheb|text=תֶּֽאֱתֶה}} (from {{GHGheb|text=אָתָה}}); {{GHGheb|text=אֵהָ֑ב}} (for {{GHGheb|text=אֵהַב}}) ''I love'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=17}}, also (four times) {{GHGheb|text=אֹהַב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mal|chapter=1|verse=2}}, &c., with suffixes {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽהֲבֵ֫הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=11|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=14|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, &c. (but only in 1st ''sing.'', otherwise {{GHGheb|text=יֶֽאֱהַב}}, &c., from {{GHGheb|text=אָהֵב}}, {{GHGheb|text=אָהַב}}); {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֵחַ֫ר|translate=and I stayed}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=5}}. The {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} of {{GHGheb|text=אָמַר}} with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} is always {{GHGheb|text=לֵאמֹר|translate=dicendo}}, for {{GHGheb|text=לֶֽאֱמֹר}}.—According to Barth ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1889, p. 179) {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫אצֶל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=25}} is to be regarded as an {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}}, without the obscuring of {{GHGheb|text=־ָא}} to ''ô'', not as {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}}, since {{GHGheb|text=אצל}} elsewhere occurs only in the {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} and {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}; on the original ''i'' in the second syllable, see above, {{GHGpar|67|p}}. For {{GHGheb|text=תְּאָכְ֫לֵהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=20|verse=26}} we should simply emend {{GHGheb|text=תֹּֽאכְל׳}}; the view that it is {{GHGterm|imperfect Pôʿēl}} (which nowhere else occurs) can, as regards the change of ''ô'' to ''ŏ'', be supported only by the very doubtful analogies of {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=62|verse=4}} (see {{GHGpar|52|q}}) and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=101|verse=5}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} (see {{GHGpar|55|b}}), while the view that it is {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} ({{GHGheb|text=תְּאָכְ׳}}={{GHGheb|text=תְּאָֽכְ׳}}={{GHGheb|text=תְּאַכְּ׳}}) rests on no analogy whatever. It would be more admissible to suppose that {{GHGheb|text=תְּאָכְ׳}} stands for {{GHGheb|text=תְּאֻכְּ׳}}, {{GHGterm|Puʿal}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=אֲכֶלְךָ}} for {{GHGheb|text=אֲכַלְּךָ}}, {{GHGpar|27|q}}); but no reason has been discovered for this departure from the natural punctuation {{GHGheb|text=תֹּאכְ׳}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|68|g}}
'''2.''' In the 1st ''pers. sing. imperfect'', where two {{GHGheb|text=א}}’s would ordinarily come together, the second (which is radical) is regularly dropped ({{GHGpar|23|f}}), as {{GHGheb|text=אֹמַר}}<ref>The regularity of this orthography indicates that the contraction of {{GHGheb|text=אַאְ}} to ''â'' in this 1st pers. occurred at a time when in the 3rd and 2nd persons the {{GHGheb|text=א}} was still audible as a consonant (which accordingly was almost always retained in writing). Nöldeke ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} xxxii. 593) infers this from the fact that also in Arabic the 3rd and 2nd persons are still written ''yăʾkŭlŭ, tăʾkŭlŭ'', but the 1st pers. ''ʾâkūlŭ'', not ''ʾăʾkŭlŭ''.</ref> (for {{GHGheb|text=אֹאמַר}}), &c., and even {{GHGterm|plene}} {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאוֹמַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=2|verse=7}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=אֽוֹמְרָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=42|verse=10}}. In the other cases, also, where the {{GHGheb|text=א}} is ordinarily regarded as ''quiescing'' in ''ô'' or ''ê'', it is only retained orthographically, and on etymological grounds. Hence the possibility of its being dropped in the following cases:—

{{GHGmargin-letter|68|h}}
Always in the contracted forms of {{GHGheb|text=אָסַף}}, as {{GHGheb|text=תֹּסֵף}} for {{GHGheb|text=תֹּאסֵף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=29}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיֹּ֫סֶף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=6|verse=1}} (but for {{GHGheb|text=יֵאָֽסֵף}}{{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=19}} read {{GHGheb|text=יֹאסִף}}={{GHGheb|text=יוֹסִף}} with the LXX); cf. also in <section end=par68 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
